question:
A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of episodic bleeding from the nose and gums and one episode of blood in her urine. She was treated with chloramphenicol 1 month ago for Rickettsia rickettsii infection. Her pulse is 130/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 105/70 mm Hg. Examination shows mucosal pallor, scattered petechiae, and ecchymoses on the extremities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 6.3 g/dL
Hematocrit 26%
Leukocyte count 900/mm3 (30% neutrophils)
Platelet count 50,000/mm3
The physician recommends a blood transfusion and informs her of the risks and benefits. Which of the following red blood cell preparations will most significantly reduce the risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Chloramphenicol treatment" -> "bone marrow suppression" -> "pancytopenia" -> "increased risk of infections" -> "concern for transfusion-related infections" -> "need to reduce infection risk" -> "leukoreduction reduces CMV risk" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Chloramphenicol treatment" -> "bone marrow suppression" -> "pancytopenia" -> "low leukocyte count" -> "increased susceptibility to infections" -> "transfusion-related CMV risk" -> "leukoreduction removes leukocytes" -> "reduces CMV risk" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Chloramphenicol treatment" -> "bone marrow suppression" -> "pancytopenia" -> "low platelet count" -> "bleeding risk" -> "transfusion needed" -> "CMV risk with transfusion" -> "leukoreduction reduces leukocyte count" -> "reduces CMV transmission" -> 92%

CHAIN: "Chloramphenicol treatment" -> "bone marrow suppression" -> "pancytopenia" -> "low hemoglobin" -> "anemia" -> "transfusion required" -> "risk of CMV infection" -> "leukoreduction reduces leukocyte count" -> "decreases CMV risk" -> 93%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and laboratory findings suggestive of aplastic anemia, likely secondary to chloramphenicol use. In this context, she requires a blood transfusion. To minimize the risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection, leukoreduction is the most effective method. CMV resides in white blood cells, and leukoreduction involves the removal of white blood cells from blood products, thereby significantly reducing the risk of CMV transmission.
